title: Scheme intersections of Borels with a common torus
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Fix a split maximal torus $T$, a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, its unipotent radical $V$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ and the quotient $Q=G/B$ with right torsor $\pi:G\to Q$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $W=N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$, acting on characters by $(w\chi)(t)=\chi(n^{-1}tn)$ for a representative $n$ of $w$. For each $\alpha\in\Phi$, let $U_\alpha$ be the root subgroup of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. For any Borel subgroup $B'\supseteq T$, write $V'=R_u(B')$ and $\Psi^+$ for its positive roots. The scheme-theoretic intersections $B\cap B'$, $V\cap B'$ and $V\cap V'$ are smooth and connected, and $V\cap B'=V\cap V'$. For any ordering of $S=\Phi^+\cap\Psi^+$ the multiplication maps
$$\prod_{\alpha\in S} U_\alpha\xrightarrow{\sim}V\cap V',\qquad \left(\prod_{\alpha\in S} U_\alpha\right)\times_F T\xrightarrow{\sim}B\cap B'$$
are isomorphisms of schemes. These assertions persist under algebraically closed extension of $F$. Empty products are $\operatorname{Spec}F$; in particular $S=\varnothing$ gives $B\cap B'=T$.

source.place: 21.66--21.68(a)--(c), pp.444--446; Proposition 21.77, formula (136), and the scheme-stabilizer computation 21.79(a), pp.448--449; opposite Borels in 21.84. Root-product extension to the common torus uses B=V semidirect T. The incorrect necessity assertion 21.68(d), identified in the appended errata, is not asserted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] to $B'$ and $T$, obtaining a regular cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to T$ with $B'=P(\lambda)$. Thus, on every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, membership in $B'(A)$ means that $t\mapsto\lambda(t)g\lambda(t)^{-1}$ extends to $\mathbf A^1_A$. Put $n_\alpha=\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle\in\mathbf Z$. Regularity gives $n_\alpha\ne0$ for every root. The Lie-algebra formula in that node, together with the definition of positive roots in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] applied to $(T,B')$, gives $\Psi^+=\{\alpha\in\Phi:n_\alpha>0\}$. In particular $S=\{\alpha\in\Phi^+:n_\alpha>0\}$.

source.place: 21.32 and 21.35, pp.434--435; limit-subgroup conventions 13.21 and 13.24, pp.261--262.

proof.text: Fix the ordering of $S$ required in the statement and extend it to an ordering of $\Phi^+$ by appending the remaining roots. By [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates], multiplication gives a $T$-equivariant scheme isomorphism $m:\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}U_\alpha\to V$. Choose the isomorphisms $u_\alpha:\mathbf G_a\to U_\alpha$ supplied by [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. They identify the source with $\operatorname{Spec}R$, $R=F[z_\alpha:\alpha\in\Phi^+]$. The conjugation formula in that node and equivariance of $m$ identify the orbit of a tuple $(a_\alpha)$ under $\lambda(t)$ with $(t^{n_\alpha}a_\alpha)$. Setting a coordinate to zero means putting the identity in that root factor.

source.place: 21.68(a) and Remark 21.69, pp.445--446; root-subgroup formula 21.19, p.431.

proof.text: For $v\in V(A)$, an extension of its $\lambda$-orbit to $G$ factors through the closed subscheme $V$. Indeed, write $G=\operatorname{Spec}H$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}(H/J)$, using the affine description of a closed immersion in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. An extension is a map $f:H\to A[t]$. Each $f(j)$ for $j\in J$ is zero in $A[t,t^{-1}]$, since the orbit over $\mathbf G_{m,A}$ lies in $V$. The inclusion $A[t]\hookrightarrow A[t,t^{-1}]$ is injective even when $A$ has nilpotents: multiplication by $t$ just shifts polynomial coefficients. Hence $f(J)=0$. Conversely an extension into $V$ is one into $G$.

source.place: 13.21--13.24, pp.261--262; restriction to a closed invariant affine subscheme, with the coefficient argument written out.

proof.text: In the coordinates of step 2, extension to $\mathbf A^1_A$ means that every Laurent monomial $t^{n_\alpha}a_\alpha$ belongs to $A[t]$. Comparing coefficients shows this holds exactly when $a_\alpha=0$ for $n_\alpha<0$; coefficients with $n_\alpha>0$ are unrestricted. Therefore $m^{-1}(V\cap B')$ is the coordinate subscheme $X_S$ cut out by the $z_\alpha$ with $\alpha\notin S$. To verify the scheme structure explicitly, let $I\subset R$ be the ideal of this pullback and $K=(z_\alpha:\alpha\notin S)$. The universal point over $R/K$ has a polynomial orbit, so $I\subseteq K$. The universal point over $R/I$ has an extending orbit by steps 1 and 3, so coefficient comparison gives $K\subseteq I$. Thus $I=K$, including all infinitesimal structure. Restricting $m$ gives the required multiplication isomorphism $\prod_{\alpha\in S}U_\alpha\simeq V\cap B'$.

source.place: 13.24, p.262, explicit Laurent-coefficient test; 21.68(a),(c), pp.445--446, root products.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] to the Borel $B'$ with the same maximal torus $T$. Every $U_\alpha$ with $\alpha\in\Psi^+$ is a subgroup of $V'$. Since $S\subseteq\Psi^+$, multiplication of the factors of $X_S$ takes values in $V'$, over every test algebra. Step 4 identifies its image as the closed subscheme $V\cap B'$, so it factors through $V\cap V'$. Conversely $V'\subseteq B'$ gives $V\cap V'\subseteq V\cap B'$. These two inclusions are inverse, being inclusions of closed subschemes of $V$. Hence $V\cap B'=V\cap V'$, and the first displayed isomorphism in the statement is proved.

source.place: 21.68(a), p.445, applied also to B prime; intersection identification in 21.79(a), p.449, made scheme-theoretic using the coordinates.

proof.text: The semidirect-product isomorphism in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] gives $V\times_F T\simeq B$, $(v,t)\mapsto vt$, with inverse $b\mapsto(bp(b)^{-1},p(b))$. Because $T\subseteq B'$, for every $A$ one has $vt\in B'(A)$ if and only if $v\in B'(A)$. Thus this isomorphism restricts to $(V\cap B')\times_F T\simeq B\cap B'$. Its inverse is the same displayed morphism restricted to $B\cap B'$; the factorization through $V\cap B'$ follows from $bp(b)^{-1}\in B'$ by the group operations. Substitute step 5 and then step 4. The resulting map is precisely $( (u_\alpha),t)\mapsto(\prod u_\alpha)t$, with the original ordering of $S$.

source.place: 21.68(b), p.445; common-torus extension of 21.68(c) and 21.79(a), using the displayed semidirect-product inverse.

proof.text: The parametrizations in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] and the split-torus condition identify the three intersections just computed with $\mathbf A_F^{|S|}$ or $\mathbf A_F^{|S|}\times_F\mathbf G_m^r$. By [def-sc-gm-ga] their coordinate algebras are $F[z_1,\ldots,z_{|S|}]$ and $F[z_1,\ldots,z_{|S|},x_1^{\pm1},\ldots,x_r^{\pm1}]$. They are finitely presented and formally smooth as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: lift each variable across a square-zero quotient, and a lift of a unit is a unit, since $(1+j)^{-1}=1-j$ for $j^2=0$. Their spectra are nonempty and connected as in [def-weil-connected-scheme]: each ring is a domain, and its zero prime belongs to every nonempty basic open, so no two nonempty opens are disjoint. This proves smoothness and connectedness without assuming them for an intersection.

source.place: 21.68(c) and 21.77, pp.445--449; explicit geometry of their root-product coordinates. Smoothness criterion: Stacks Definition 02H0, as stated in def-sbc-smooth-morphisms.

proof.text: For an algebraically closed extension $E/F$, restriction to commutative $E$-algebras preserves every functor calculation above. More explicitly, the equations $z_\alpha=0$ for $\alpha\notin S$, the multiplication maps, their coordinate inverses, and the semidirect-product inverse in step 6 all extend by scalars. Intersections commute with this operation because they are fibre products: a point is a pair of points with equal image in $G$. The coordinate rings in step 7 simply replace $F$ by $E$, so the same smoothness and connectedness calculation applies. Our ordering of $S$ was arbitrary at step 2. If $S=\varnothing$, its coordinate product is $\operatorname{Spec}F$, and steps 4--6 give $V\cap B'=V\cap V'=1$ and $B\cap B'=T$. This also covers $G=T$ and the trivial group.

source.place: 13.24 and 21.69, pp.262,446; scalar extension and empty products in the explicit coordinate argument.

proof_origin.place: Explicit common-torus intersection argument using 21.32, 21.68(a),(b), 21.69 and the Laurent-coefficient limit test of 13.24; verifies the conclusions of 21.77 and 21.79(a) on all test algebras.
